To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

X-ray diffraction measurements of relaxed InGaAss/GaAs heterojunctions grown on (100) substrates misoriented with respect to the (110) axis show that the epitaxial layers are tilted by a few degrees with respect to the substrate.
the X-ray diffraction profile from an InGaAss/GaAs heterojunction grown on a (1 00) substrate with an offcut of 2 degrees toward (110) is strongly dependent on the azimuthal angle.
the lattice planes of InGaAs grown on a (001) substrate misoriented toward [110] are reoriented by an angle of about 1 degrees with respect to the substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of InGaAs on GaAs substrates misoriented toward (110).
the growth of InGaAs/GalnP heterostructures on (100) misoriented substrates, the study of the strain relaxation in such layers, and the characterization of the strain state of the layers.
the development of a method of measuring the misorientation of a substrate by X-ray diffraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tilt angle alpha is a function of the misorientation epsilon and the lattice mismatch delta between the substrate and the layer.

, in the case of lattice mismatched epitaxy on misoriented substrats, the tilt angle is not only a measure of the relaxation of the epitaxial film, but it is also an indication of the reorientation of the epitaxially deposited lattice planes.
the lattice mismatch strain is relieved by the formation of a network of dislocations, which in this case are not confined to a single plane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the X-ray measurements of the tilt angle are consistent with the strain relaxation mechanism proposed for lattice mismatched heterostructures.
we have demonstrated a new method of measuring the misorientation of the substrate, which is important for the growth of relaxed layers on misoriented substrats.
we have shown that X-ray diffraction is a useful and accurate technique for the characterization of relaxed InGaAS heterostructures grown by MBE on misoriented GaAS substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tilt angle alpha is not a fixed value but varies with the azimuthal orientation.
the strain-relaxation mechanisms in lattice mismatched layers grown on mis-oriented substrates can be studied by X-ray diffraction.
X-ray diffraction can be used as a nondestructive method for the accurate determination of the misorientation angle and tilt angle in lattice mismatched epitaxy.
